## Appearance

Jane Andrews has an appearance that is described as neat, sensible, and plain.

_Sources: [v3 ch.Autumn P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004)_

## Personality

Jane Andrews is a steady, practical, and unflappable individual, known for her sensible, lady-like, and amiable nature. Characterized by a placid demeanor, she is skilled in cooking. Early on, she was motivated to dedicate her life to teaching for a salary and never marry, though she later resigned from her teaching position with plans to go West.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Queen’s Class Is Organized P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 CHAPTER XXXI. Where the Brook and River Meet P30](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0030), [v1 CHAPTER XXXII. ## History

Jane Andrews grew up in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) and attended the local school, where she joined a story club with her classmates [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md), and Ruby. She later attended Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy) alongside [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and Ruby. On the final day of their school term, Jane was brought to tears during her teacher's farewell speech and had to borrow a handkerchief from her brother. Later, Jane attended a charity concert at the [White Sands Hotel](../codex/places.md#white-sands-hotel), traveling to the event and returning in a carriage driven by her brother [Billy](../character/billy-andrews.md). After earning her teaching certificate at Queen's, she taught at [Newbridge](../codex/places.md#newbridge) school, earning a spot on the Inspector's Roll of Honor, before eventually resigning from her teaching position in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) to teach on the western prairies. While living in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), Jane actively participated in the local Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvers) and joined her friends for outings, including exploring a hidden garden. She also personally delivered a marriage proposal to [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) on behalf of her brother [Billy](../character/billy-andrews.md), though [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) rejected the unromantic offer, leading Jane to react coldly. Jane eventually married a wealthy millionaire and went to [Europe](../codex/places.md#europe) for her wedding tour.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P4](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0004), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P28](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0028), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P33](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0033), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P34](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0034), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P38](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0038), +23 more_

## Quotes

> “Of course it would be romantic,” conceded Jane Andrews, “but I know I couldn’t keep still. I’d be popping up every minute or so to see where I was and if I wasn’t drifting too far out. And you know, Anne, that would spoil the effect.”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P2](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0002)

> “I don’t know how you’re going to prevent him,” exclaimed Jane bitterly. “Everybody knows what Judson Parker is. He’d do anything for money. He hasn’t a spark of public spirit or any sense of the beautiful.”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P41](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0041)

> "Wouldn’t it be nice to have three wishes granted you . . . or even only one? What would you wish for, girls, if you could have a wish granted? I’d wish to be rich and beautiful and clever."
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 XIII A Golden Picnic P32](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0032)

> “Oh, Anne,” gasped Jane, as they fled to the girls’ dressing room amid hearty cheers. “Oh, Anne I’m so proud! Isn’t it splendid?”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream P8](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0008)

> "I’ll whip my pupils when they’re naughty. It’s the shortest and easiest way of convincing them."
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 IV Different Opinions P14](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0014)
